answer: Each new AI agent receives a cryptographic token whose proof‑of‑work must be solved on a dedicated jetty of compute nodes, the results recorded in an immutable grove of Merkle roots that form the system’s haven of verified identities. If a batch of identical grading answers appears, a planted honeypot flags the submitters as a Sybil group, forcing an attacker to spend a full puzzle’s CPU and separate hardware for every fake ID, making the cost grow linearly with the number of identities.
